safety_verdicts.content: Patient reports shortness of breath while running.
safety_verdicts.eval_reasoning: Gold specifies SOB while running; generated facts do not mention exertional/running trigger.
safety_verdicts.clinical_rationale: Omitting that dyspnea occurs while running removes an exertional trigger that helps gauge asthma control and severity. This can lead to under-recognition of exercise-induced symptoms and less targeted counseling or treatment adjustment.

safety_verdicts.content: Patient has needed to use the blue inhaler twice a day.
safety_verdicts.eval_reasoning: Gold states blue inhaler needed twice daily; generated only states 'daily' and evenings, without the twice-daily frequency.
safety_verdicts.clinical_rationale: Not documenting that the reliever is needed twice daily can understate current symptom burden and short-acting beta-agonist reliance, which are key markers of poor control/exacerbation. This may delay escalation of therapy or safety-netting.
